land.text: Mingrelia (Samegrelo) with Lechkhumi and Svaneti, as the Dadiani princes held it when Georgia split into 'three kingdoms and several principalities'

predecessors.note: The infobox lists the Kingdom of Georgia and the Kingdom of Imereti as predecessors; the page does not call the Dadiani Imereti's vassals; the Imereti page says Mingrelia 'declared independence from Imereti' (undated), and Mingrelia's own text dates its independence to 1557 ('established as an independent Principality ... with Levan I Dadiani serving as a hereditary mtavari').

land.text: the principality, 'abolished, by Russia in 1867' (annexation 4 January 1867); Niko I renounced his rights in 1868 and the state 'became a Russian district until 1917'

successors.note: Russian vassal from 1803 (infobox: 'Vassal of the Russian Empire (1803-1867)'). Cliopatria's row ends in 1810, 57 years earlier.

capitals.name: Zugdidi
capitals.note: Infobox: capital Zugdidi, no years given; the page does not say where the Dadiani sat before it.

correction.text: Mingrelia as Cliopatria's first shape, carried back to 1463

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the infobox says 'Established: 1463' (Cliopatria starts 1468). The 1468 shape is carried back unchanged.

13,251 km2, the Mingrelian plain plus the uplands to the Svaneti ridge and Lechkhumi (the 1865 population table counts Lechkhumi, Senaki and Zugdidi districts). The page gives no area. 'Mingrelia was established as an independent Principality in 1557 with Levan I Dadiani serving as a hereditary mtavari'; the shape is unchanged by it.
13,203 km2, a 47 km2 change on the coast, unexplained; the page is silent on the 1570s (the Ottoman fort at Tskhumi lies in Abkhazia). Unverified: page silent.

New keyframe for 1579-1611, which Cliopatria leaves empty (its Ottoman row probably covers it). The page does not interrupt the principality ('It remained independent until it became a subject to Imperial Russia in 1803'). The 1572 shape is kept.
13,203 km2; page silent on 1612-1699. Unverified: page silent.

8,303 km2 (-37%): the northwest goes. Samurzakano page: 'in 1705 three brothers of the Abkhazian ruling family' divided their land, the third taking 'the southern part (from the Ghalidzga to the R. Enguri)', 'roughly equivalent to the modern Gali District'. That the strip belonged to Mingrelia before is a reading from Cliopatria's pair of shapes (Abkhazia +4,400 km2 in 1700), not a statement of either page.

5,820 km2 (-30%): Upper Svaneti and the northeast go. Svaneti page: the Dadeshkeliani 'emerged as the eventual winners by the 1720s' and 'its territory west of the Enguri became the Principality of Svaneti'; Cliopatria's Svaneti starts in 1721. Lower Svaneti was 'gradually subjugated by the Dadiani princes of Mingrelia' (same page), so the Dadiani kept a share.

5,154 km2 (-11%): the western coast (west of 41.79E) goes, the same year Cliopatria's Guria and Abkhazia lose coast and an Ottoman row appears beside Mingrelia. No page dates or explains it. Unverified: page silent.
5,107 km2, a 1% change; Solomon I page: after the 1768-1774 war 'he forced his autonomist vassals, the princes of Mingrelia and Guria, into submission' (no territory).
5,036 km2, a 1% change. Unverified: page silent.

5,036 km2 for 1809-1810. Infobox: 'Vassal of the Russian Empire (1803-1867)'; the 1803 patronage treaty 'sought Russian protection against Imeretia and Abkhazia'. The territory is unchanged; Cliopatria ends the row in 1810.

correction.text: the principality as it stood in 1809, carried to 1866

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1811-1866: Cliopatria ends Mingrelia in 1810 but the principality lasted until 4 January 1867 as a Russian vassal ('the principality was abolished, by Russia in 1867'). The 1809 shape is carried forward unchanged; the vassal tint belongs to the Russian dossier, and Cliopatria's Russian Empire row may already contain this land.

region.text: Mingrelia with Lechkhumi and the Svaneti ridge, seat at Zugdidi

ledger.note: 1463: the Dadiani principality of Mingrelia appears when Georgia splits. Infobox: 'Established: 1463'; 'The principality arose from a pact and treaty among Georgian rulers that split Georgia into three kingdoms and several principalities'; 'Mingrelia was established as an independent Principality in 1557 with Levan I Dadiani serving as a hereditary mtavari (Prince)', the only independence date the text gives.

region.text: the strip 'from the Ghalidzga to the R. Enguri', roughly the modern Gali District

ledger.note: c. 1700-1705: Abkhazia takes the Ghalidzga-Enguri strip. Samurzakano page: 'in 1705 three brothers of the Abkhazian ruling family, surnamed Chachba' divided their land, 'the third, Murzaqan, the southern part (from the Ghalidzga to the R. Enguri)'. Whether it was Mingrelian before is a reading from Cliopatria (Mingrelia -4,900 km2, Abkhazia +4,400 in 1700); the year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: the Svaneti ridge and upper Enguri, detached from the Mingrelian shape

ledger.note: 1720s: Upper Svaneti becomes its own principality. 'The Dadeshkeliani emerged as the eventual winners by the 1720s' in the struggle over the Enguri, and 'its territory west of the Enguri became the Principality of Svaneti'; Lower Svaneti 'was gradually subjugated by the Dadiani princes of Mingrelia'. Year 1721 is Cliopatria's first Svaneti shape.

region.text: the coast west of 41.79E, Poti and Anaklia

ledger.note: 1727: the Poti-Anaklia coast leaves the Mingrelian shape (-660 km2). Page silent. Read as an Ottoman gain because an Ottoman row appears beside Mingrelia from 1727 in Cliopatria's neighbours, and Guria and Abkhazia lose coast the same year.

region.text: the whole principality, a Russian vassal since 1803

ledger.note: 1867: Russia abolishes the Principality of Mingrelia. Infobox: 'Annexation by Imperial Russia: January 4, 1867'; 'the principality was abolished, by Russia in 1867'; Prince Niko I 'officially renounced his rights to the throne in 1868'.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1806-1812)
wars.outcome: Russia won; the Treaty of Bucharest (28 May 1812) returned Poti, Anapa and Akhalkalaki to Turkey. The war page lists Mingrelia only among the belligerents and map labels.
wars.note: Mingrelia was already Russia's vassal (1803, Mingrelia page). No territory dated.

wars.name: Russo-Turkish War (1828-1829)
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Adrianople (14 September 1829) has the Sultan recognize Russia's possession of 'Georgia (with Imeretia, Mingrelia, Guria)'.
wars.note: The Mingrelia page does not mention this war.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines on the pages. The Svaneti, Abkhazian and Imeretian frontiers are approximate; the Ottoman coast (Poti, Anaklia) is the least certain.

sources.title: Principality of Mingrelia

notes: Page budget: up to 5, six opened. The Mingrelia article is short and has no history section: it dates 1463 (infobox), 1557 (independence under Levan I Dadiani), 1803, 1867 and 1868 only, and gives no area. Cliopatria: the row ends 1810 although the principality lasted to 1867 (new keyframe 1811-1866); no shape for 1579-1611 (new keyframe). The 1727 coastal loss and the shrinkage of 1775/1788 are Cliopatria shape changes no page explains (confidence 1 or left unverified). Vassalage for the suzerain dossiers: Imereti (overlord until 1557, when 'Mingrelia was established as an independent Principality'; and again after the 1768-1774 war, 'forced his autonomist vassals ... into submission'; recorded in the Imereti dossier); Ottoman (Poti coast, 1727 on, nothing dated on the pages); Russian Empire from 1803 (infobox 'Vassal of the Russian Empire (1803-1867)') to 4 January 1867. Disagreement: infobox 1463 against the text's 1557 independence; 1463 chosen as the start because Cliopatria and the neighbouring principalities (Guria, Abkhazia, Svaneti) all begin from the 1463 Chikhori break. Region names the gazetteer may lack: Samurzakano (region).
